terribly.lineNext: When you question their sacred texts
stanza: Oh, their religions are the best
They worship themselves yet they're totally obsessed
With risen zombies, celestial virgins, magic tricks
These unbelievable outfits
And they get terribly upset
When you question their sacred texts
Written by woman-hating epileptics

terribly.linePrev: A cord or two — which you chop, and you stack in your barrow
terribly.line: And it is terribly good to carry water and chop wood
terribly.lineNext: Streaked with soot, heavy-booted and wild-eyed;
stanza: And then the system of strings tugs on the tip of my wings
(cut from cardboard and old magazines):
Makes me warble and rise, like a sparrow
And in the place where I stood, there is a circle of wood —
A cord or two — which you chop, and you stack in your barrow
And it is terribly good to carry water and chop wood
Streaked with soot, heavy-booted and wild-eyed;
As I crash through the rafters
And the ropes and the pulleys trail after
And the holiest belfry burns sky-high

terribly.linePrev: Can you imagine us years from today, sharing a parkbench quietly
terribly.line: How terribly strange to be seventy
terribly.lineNext: Old friends, memory brushes the same years, silently sharing the same fears
stanza: 1 ContributorOld Friends LyricsOld friends, old friends sat on their parkbench…
A newspaper blowin' through the grass
Falls on the round toes of the high shoes of the old friends
Old friends, winter companions, the old men
Lost in their overcoats, waiting for the sun
The sounds of the city sifting through trees
Settles like dust on the shoulders of the old friends
Can you imagine us years from today, sharing a parkbench quietly
How terribly strange to be seventy
Old friends, memory brushes the same years, silently sharing the same fears
